cards.heading: The protocol history
cards.body: WEP (RC4) is broken and must never be used. WPA (TKIP) was a stop-gap. WPA2 (802.11i) uses AES-CCMP and is the baseline. WPA3 adds SAE, mandatory protected management frames (PMF) and stronger GCMP-256 encryption in its 192-bit Enterprise mode.
cards.example:
WEP  RC4         broken
WPA  TKIP        deprecated
WPA2 AES-CCMP    baseline
WPA3 SAE + PMF   current

cards.heading: Personal and Enterprise
cards.body: Personal mode uses a pre-shared key (passphrase) everyone knows. Enterprise mode uses 802.1X/EAP with a RADIUS server, so every user has their own credentials and access can be revoked per user.

cards.heading: WPA3 SAE
cards.body: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals replaces WPA2-Personal's PSK handshake. It resists offline dictionary attacks against captured handshakes and gives forward secrecy: capturing traffic today and learning the passphrase later doesn't decrypt it.

cards.heading: WPA2-PSK in the WLC GUI
cards.body: WLANs > select the WLAN > Security > Layer 2. Set Layer 2 Security to WPA+WPA2, tick WPA2 Policy with AES encryption, set Authentication Key Management to PSK, choose the PSK format (ASCII) and enter a passphrase of 8-63 characters. Apply and save.
cards.example:
Security > Layer 2
  Layer 2 Security: WPA+WPA2
  WPA2 Policy: ✓   Encryption: AES
  Auth Key Mgmt: PSK   Format: ASCII
  PSK: ********************
